theory.title: Negotiation, Diplomacy and Institutional Communication
theory.explanation: This mission develops advanced diplomatic negotiation. Effective C2 communication requires writers and speakers to make purpose, audience, evidence and degree of certainty explicit. Analyse the context before choosing a register; distinguish established information from interpretation; organise complex material so that decisions and qualifications remain visible.
theory.tip: Use precise terminology, attribute claims, qualify uncertainty and make the requested action explicit.

patterns.label: Define purpose and audience
patterns.pattern: Identify what the audience needs to know or decide.
examples: State the decision required before presenting supporting detail.

patterns.label: Support and qualify
patterns.pattern: Connect each claim to evidence and state relevant limitations.
examples: The findings suggest a pattern, although the sample is not representative.

patterns.label: Structure for action
patterns.pattern: Use signposting, headings and explicit ownership.
examples: The recommendation is assigned to a named lead for review by an agreed date.

patterns.label: Review for integrity
patterns.pattern: Check terminology, attribution, tone and consistency.
examples: Distinguish verified outcomes from projected benefits.

content.passage:
Two departments were negotiating a shared data policy. One wanted a single reporting format to reduce administrative costs; the other argued that a uniform template would obscure differences in how its services collected information. Their first meeting ended in an impasse because each side treated its preferred format as a red line.

A facilitator asked them to separate positions from interests. Both departments wanted comparable results, but one prioritised efficiency while the other needed methodological transparency. They agreed to a common core dataset with a supplementary section for service-specific measures. The arrangement involved a trade-off: the reporting process would be slightly longer, but the comparison would be more meaningful.

The wording of the agreement described the arrangement as provisional and set a review date. Neither side claimed complete victory. The facilitator noted that diplomatic communication does not require disguising disagreement; it requires making the remaining disagreement manageable, recording reciprocal commitments and clarifying what would trigger a revision.
